title: Case E — Niigata district
summary: Real district in Niigata at 1:250, before and after a 60 m high-rise and two 18 m mid-rises; pedestrian-height velocity ratio (thermistor), 16 wind directions.

configuration.district: Niigata City urban area near the Shinano River; dense low-rise stock (median top 6 m, max 30 m)

states.bc: before construction (sites of A, B, C empty)
states.ac: after construction of A (60 m high-rise), B and C (18 m mid-rises)

configuration.measurement_height_note: 2 m full scale = 0.008 m model scale
configuration.normalisation: velocity ratio = mean scalar speed at 2 m / inflow velocity at 15.9 m (the Niigata meteorological station height); U(15.9 m) = 0.504531 x UR = 3.935 m/s with UR = 7.8 m/s at ZR = 250 m
configuration.instrument: thermistor anemometer, 100 Hz, 60 s per point, mean scalar wind speed

frame.origin: centre of the reproduced area, ground plane
frame.wind_direction_rotation: meteorological FROM-direction, clockwise from north; the compass name is the direction the wind comes from (N = 0 deg blows toward -y, E = 90 deg toward -x). This case keeps its geographic frame instead of '+x along the wind' because the district is real and its coordinates are the data's.

inflow_fit.method: the workbook publishes z/ZR, U/UR, k/UR^2 with ZR = 250 m, UR = 7.8 m/s and epsilon = Cmu^0.5 k dU/dz (Cmu = 0.09); de-normalised to full-scale metres and m/s here
inflow_fit.log_law: does not fit: kappa = 0.41 fits reach 5.3-9.4 % max error over the relevant height range and overshoot U(15.9 m) by 4-7 %
inflow_fit.note: derived during scoping, not published by AIJ

fit.method: the workbook publishes z/ZR, U/UR, k/UR^2 with ZR = 250 m, UR = 7.8 m/s and epsilon = Cmu^0.5 k dU/dz (Cmu = 0.09); de-normalised to full-scale metres and m/s here
fit.log_law: does not fit: kappa = 0.41 fits reach 5.3-9.4 % max error over the relevant height range and overshoot U(15.9 m) by 4-7 %
fit.note: derived during scoping, not published by AIJ

benchmark_data.note: the measured profile and the fit of it are the benchmark's data as cleaned here; everything under `recommended` is a choice

recommended.status: RECOMMENDED by this repository (not part of the benchmark): no log law fits this case (inflow_fit says why); use the measured approach-flow profile as a tabulated inlet (approach_flow.csv). Any inlet may be submitted; say which in submission.yaml
recommended.profile: U(z) and, where published, k(z) tabulated from approach_flow.csv; epsilon = Cmu^0.5 k dU/dz where k is published, else from your own closure
recommended.openfoam: fixedProfile (OpenFOAM.org) with the table, or timeVaryingMappedFixedValue: cases/{id}/inflow_openfoam.txt holds the table

flow_direction.meaning: meteorological FROM-direction theta, clockwise from north: flowDir (-sin theta, -cos theta, 0)

eddy3d_runs.inlet: manual (the workbook's tabulated profile, ZR 250 m, UR 7.8 m/s)

inflow.domain: the extents, blockage and cell sizes of Eddy3D's domains are not in its snapshots and are not stated here; mesh.cells and the scale are, where the snapshot has them

probes.columns_meaning: the key columns of a scored file (point_id with config, campaign, instrument, run and wind_direction_deg as the case has them), x, y, z in m (case frame), and scored_as: the families the row is scored in (vector, k, thermistor_bracket, concentration, theta, joined by +)

scoring.U_ref_meaning: the table holds Vs/U(15.9 m) (U(15.9 m) = 3.935 m/s); give ratios

scored_as.vector: U, V, W and the speed |U| against the split-fibre, LDV or hot-wire components (velocity.U, velocity.V, velocity.W, speed)
scored_as.thermistor_bracket: a mean scalar speed (thermistor, cup or sonic anemometer) against |U| (vs.vector) and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) (vs.scalar)

scoring.conventions: velocities and the speed over U_ref, k over U_ref^2 (Cases E, F and G publish ratios already); U, V, W, |U| and the thermistor bracket scored as signed velocities (FAC2's ratio keeps the sign; hit rate D = 0.25, W = 0.05); k by the plain definitions (D = 0.25 only); a thermistor, cup or sonic reading (a mean scalar speed) scored against |U| (vs.vector) and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) (vs.scalar), the two ends of its bracket; c* = C/c0 with one detection limit per case, 1e-3 of the largest measured value; theta = (T_floor - T)/(T_floor - T_H) scored like a positive velocity. The same conventions score the served Eddy3D results (docs/validation/method.md).
scoring.tool: uv run python validation/score_submissions.py <folder>, from a checkout of the repository (pyproject.toml)

metric_meaning.MeanObserved: mean of the measured, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.MeanPredicted: mean of the modelled, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.Fb: fractional bias, 2 (mean_obs - mean_pred) / (mean_obs + mean_pred); positive = model low
metric_meaning.Fac2: fraction of points within a factor of two (harsh near zero for sign-changing V and W)
metric_meaning.HitRate: fraction of points within D = 0.25 relative or W = 0.05 U_H absolute
metric_meaning.GeometricPairs: pairs with both values positive (used for Mg/Vg)
metric_meaning.null: a metric that is undefined for the data (for example Mg and Vg when no pair has both values positive; Fb, Nmse and Nad of a signed velocity component of Case H or I whose observed and predicted means are not both positive)

known_issues: The velocity ratio is normalised by the inflow velocity at 15.9 m (= 3.935 m/s), NOT by U_H and NOT by UR = 7.8 m/s. A prior Eddy3D comparison in the folder divided by the wrong reference and came out low by a factor of 2.048 (FAC2 0.338 -> 0.863 once rescaled, R unchanged at 0.661).
All 2560 published ratios are integer multiples of 0.0198204 (55 distinct levels): the data's own resolution is +/-0.0099, 3.1 % of the median value and about 10 % at the lowest points.
The readme describes AF_caseE.csv, RS_caseE.csv and BD_caseE.stl, but this repository holds only the .3dm, .ghx, .xls and the MP drawing; everything here is extracted from the workbook and the 3dm.

case-e.3dm is FULL-SCALE metres (MP_caseE.png is drawn at model scale, +/-0.8 m). Use layers 'buildings' (5,015 meshes, before construction) and 'buildings_new_construction' (3 prisms); exclude the map plate on the Japanese-named general layer, the terrain plates (the site is flat) and 'probes'.
case-e.3dm: 1,563 of 8,436 triangles (18.5 %) of the building meshes are wound against their neighbours; all are re-wound here.

Do not take the measurement coordinates from the 3dm's 'probes' layer: its 80 spheres sit a median 2.31 m (max 21 m) from the workbook's points, which are authoritative (all 80 fall in open space, min 0.83 m from a building edge).

The measured quantity is a scalar (thermistor) speed; a RANS |U| is biased low against it in a dense canopy. The construction signal (ac - bc) is largest for SW (mean |d| 0.2155) and smallest for SSE (0.093).
